units.text: INT. NOTARY'S OFFICE - DAY
A cramped room above a dry cleaner.
Steam pipes bang.
A wall calendar shows a lighthouse.
One desk, three chairs, a stack of papers between them.
GLORIA TANAKA-REYES, 50s, in a navy suit, sits rigid, hands flat on the desk.
LEONARD FITCH, 60s, the notary, adjusts his bow tie and squints at the will.
EZEKIEL "ZEKE" TANAKA-REYES, 30s, her younger brother, slumps in the third chair, jiggling his knee.
The house goes to the surviving child.
units.name: LEONARD

units.text: There are two of us.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: The surviving child who occupied the house for the last five years.
units.name: LEONARD

units.text: That's me.
units.name: ZEKE

units.text: That's you because I was working.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: I was there when she fell.
units.name: ZEKE

units.text: We were all there when she fell.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: Not you.
units.name: ZEKE

units.text: Say that again.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: Please. The language of the will is clear.
units.name: LEONARD

units.text: Then read the clause about the debts.
units.name: GLORIA

units.text: The debts also go to the occupant.
units.name: LEONARD

units.text: Wait, what debts?
units.name: ZEKE

units.text: Leonard slides a page across.
Zeke stares at it.
His knee stops.
Oh, Mama. What did you do.
units.name: ZEKE
